## Desktop app

| Computer | Download |
|---|---|
| Mac with Apple chip (M1, M2, …) | [sshproxy-macos-arm64.zip](https://github.com/zzn01/sshproxy/releases/latest/download/sshproxy-macos-arm64.zip) |
| Mac with Intel chip | [sshproxy-macos-amd64.zip](https://github.com/zzn01/sshproxy/releases/latest/download/sshproxy-macos-amd64.zip) |
| Windows (most PCs) | [sshproxy-windows-amd64.exe](https://github.com/zzn01/sshproxy/releases/latest/download/sshproxy-windows-amd64.exe) |
| Windows on ARM (e.g. Snapdragon laptops) | [sshproxy-windows-arm64.exe](https://github.com/zzn01/sshproxy/releases/latest/download/sshproxy-windows-arm64.exe) |
| Linux (most PCs) | [sshproxy-linux-amd64](https://github.com/zzn01/sshproxy/releases/latest/download/sshproxy-linux-amd64) |
| Linux on ARM (e.g. Raspberry Pi) | [sshproxy-linux-arm64](https://github.com/zzn01/sshproxy/releases/latest/download/sshproxy-linux-arm64) |

The apps aren't code-signed, so macOS and Windows warn the first time; the [README](https://github.com/zzn01/sshproxy#2-open-it) explains how to open them.

## Command line

`sshproxy-cli-<os>-<arch>`, for example `sshproxy-cli-linux-amd64`. Rename it to `sshproxy` and put it on your `PATH`. See [Command line](https://github.com/zzn01/sshproxy#command-line).
